findings.summary: The proposed durable `work lane` duplicates an existing durable task-envelope owner without a reuse or migration decision.
evidence: The proposal introduces `work lane` as a durable invocation entity and a new subject-bound invocation record (`charness-artifacts/ideation/2026-08-24-consumer-friction-and-file-backed-lanes.md:61`, `:171`).

The current CLI already owns repo-local durable task state under `.charness/tasks/*.json`, with claim, submit, abort, status, result summary, and artifact references (`charness:3173`, `:3252`, `:3296`, `:3344`, `:3378`, `:5746`).

The existing task schema is too weak for provenance-preserving external execution, but that is an extension seam: its submission currently carries only summary and artifacts (`charness:3330`). The decision artifact does not inspect or disposition this owner.
findings.action: Before Q1 locks a new command/entity, choose one canonical durable run-state owner. Prefer extending `charness task` with invocation identity, terminal receipt, and typed result references, composed with the existing worker and worktree commands. If a distinct lane store is necessary, specify retirement or migration of `.charness/tasks` and prove why composition cannot satisfy the capability.

findings.summary: The claimed single host process/receipt substrate has no canonical implementation or field-ownership migration, so Option B can ship a third normalizer and a second configuration family.
evidence: The proposal acknowledges both the Python reviewer runtime and the JavaScript Codex eval runtime (`charness-artifacts/ideation/2026-08-24-consumer-friction-and-file-backed-lanes.md:109`) and requires one process boundary (`:188`), but the rollout only repairs and exposes the reviewer runner (`:265`); it does not migrate the eval runtime.

The Python runtime independently constructs Codex/Claude argv and hardcodes read-only execution (`skills/shared/scripts/reviewer_worker_runtime.py:180`), while the JavaScript runtime independently owns sandbox, model, reasoning effort, isolated `CODEX_HOME`, and auth behavior (`scripts/agent-runtime/codex-eval-runtime.mjs:15`, `:74`). Both implementations are exported because packaging copies `skills/shared` and the full `scripts` tree (`scripts/packaging_lib.py:248`, `:300`).

Tracked reviewer backend/tier/timeout already belong to `.agents/critique-adapter.yaml:13`, while the existing ignored repo-local capability family belongs at `.charness/local/capability.json` (`docs/runtime-capability-contract.md:29`). The proposal asks for one tracked execution adapter and one ignored policy surface (`charness-artifacts/ideation/2026-08-24-consumer-friction-and-file-backed-lanes.md:128`, `:223`) without assigning or migrating these existing fields.
findings.action: Make the spec name one executable host-adapter/process contract and one field-level configuration ownership table. Require reviewer execution and Codex eval execution to delegate to that owner, migrate `reviewer_runner` fields deliberately, and extend or explicitly reject the existing capability-local family for backend/auth/grant settings. Acceptance must fail while two independent argv/env/auth normalizers or two authorities for the same field remain.

findings.summary: `input-drift` is required as a terminal state, but the proposed common boundary is not given observable inputs from which it can compute that verdict.
evidence: The invocation envelope carries subject paths, an input-manifest digest, worktree identity, and instruction identities (`charness-artifacts/ideation/2026-08-24-consumer-friction-and-file-backed-lanes.md:173`), while the receipt vocabulary promises `input-drift` (`:199`).

Current worker preflight checks only workspace/input-file existence, timeout, path distinctness, and stale artifacts (`skills/shared/scripts/reviewer_worker_runtime.py:145`). Result validation merely compares identities repeated by the model result with opaque identities supplied by the caller (`skills/shared/scripts/reviewer_worker_runtime.py:111`).

The terminal receipt records those opaque identities and hashes only prompt/schema/output (`skills/shared/scripts/reviewer_worker_runtime.py:287`); it does not receive or re-observe the subject manifest. The review-specific packet verifier exists elsewhere, but investigation and implementation carriers have no equivalent owner in the proposed architecture.
findings.action: Assign drift observation to an executable layer. Pass a canonical readable input manifest to the process boundary, hash it immediately before launch and after collection, and test a same-looking successful result while a subject, instruction, local-policy file, or expected worktree identity changes. That run must end `input-drift`, never delivered; self-reported result identities cannot satisfy the test.

findings.summary: The rollout makes the repaired proof surface dogfood itself without reserving an independent acceptance channel.
evidence: Step 3 repairs the reviewer runner, exposes the new command, and then dogfoods that command on the task-completing fresh-eye review of the same program (`charness-artifacts/ideation/2026-08-24-consumer-friction-and-file-backed-lanes.md:265`).

The combined report is the surface that converts delivery, provenance, ledger state, and semantic verdict into `approval_eligible` (`skills/shared/scripts/reviewer_worker_report.py:188`). A successful self-run therefore exercises the candidate surface but cannot independently establish that its approval rendering is trustworthy.

The repo contract requires a second bounded round when a slice changes verdict logic and the first round causes repairs (`AGENTS.md:38`). The dependency order does not identify a pre-existing worker, typed reviewer, or other distinct observer for either initial acceptance or the conditional second round.
findings.action: Reverse the proof dependency: review the new command and any repaired approval path through a pre-existing independent channel, then treat dogfood through the candidate command as supplementary behavior evidence. Reserve a second independent round if the first round repairs verdict logic; do not let the candidate command's own `approval_eligible` output close its acceptance.

next_move: Keep Option B provisional, but tighten the spec before implementation: disposition `charness task` as the durable-state owner, name and migrate to one host execution/config authority, define executable pre/post input-drift observation, and rewrite the rollout so an existing independent reviewer approves the candidate surface before its dogfood result is trusted.
non_claims: No files were modified and no descendants were spawned.
The supplied packet SHA-256 was verified against the JSON prepare packet, and its reviewed-input binding verified current. The Markdown render itself does not have the supplied packet SHA-256.
No Codex or Claude backend was launched, so the relative-path concern and nested `CODEX_HOME` behavior were not reproduced as bugs in this review.
GitHub issue counts, current issue dispositions, installed-6.4.0 behavior, and Ceal adoption were not independently reverified.
No broad quality suite, packaging sync, mutation run, or performance/cost benchmark was executed.
This review does not claim Option B is fundamentally wrong; it blocks locking the current ownership and rollout contract.
Counterweight triage was intentionally not performed because the parent owns that separate pass.
